mainTopic: The end of the perek הלוקח עובר פרתו (בכור in one respect, like אביי), and the new משנה about an animal bought from a גוי, including when we follow a רוב
overview: The amud opens by finishing a debate about an animal that is a בכור in only one respect. רבינא says such an animal still counts as a בכור, so he uses the extra word 'בכור' to exclude an animal born after a יוצא דופן. רב אחא מדפתי shows that a female born by caesarean and then a male born naturally would remain unexcluded under that approach. So the גמרא concludes like אביי: a בכור in one respect is not a בכור. That ends the perek הלוקח עובר פרתו. A new perek opens with a משנה about buying an animal from a גוי when no one knows whether it already gave birth. רבי ישמעאל rules by the mother's age, and רבי עקיבא answers that signs of pregnancy also exempt an animal, so only real knowledge decides. The גמרא then asks why an older animal is only a ספק, since most animals give birth in their first year. It suggests that even רבנן follow only a majority that is in front of us, but the case of minors and יבום disproves this. The amud ends as רבא begins a new answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'firstborn' cannot be needed to exclude a male born after a female
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rules out one possible job for the word 'בכור': excluding a male that came out after a female. That case is already covered by the words 'פטר רחם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the word 'firstborn' were meant to exclude a case where a female came out of the womb before the male, that is already learned from the words 'that which opens the womb'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא is looking for what the extra word 'בכור' comes to teach. He first rejects one possible answer. This step sets up his real answer in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a female came out of the womb first, the male did not 'open the womb'. So 'פטר רחם' already excludes him. That means the word 'בכור' must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude (a case from the law)
'that which opens the womb': the first to come out of the womb
a female
it is derived / it comes out (from a verse)

phrases.english: If it comes to exclude
a case where a female came out before it
that is derived from 'that which opens the womb'!
phrases.notes: A male born after a female did not open the womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְמַעוֹטֵי הֵיכָא דְּיָצְתָה נְקֵבָה לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבינא's position on the previous amud, where he holds that a בכור in one respect is still a בכור.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects one possible use of the extra word 'בכור'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That use is already covered by 'פטר רחם', so the word would add nothing.

steps.title: So 'firstborn' excludes an animal born after a caesarean sibling
steps.stepSummary: רבינא concludes that the word 'בכור' excludes an animal born naturally after an older sibling came out by caesarean.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that the word 'firstborn' comes to exclude a case where an animal comes out after an animal born by caesarean section.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives his answer: the extra word 'בכור' teaches that an animal born after a יוצא דופן is not a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such an animal did open the womb, so 'פטר רחם' alone would make it holy. Since רבינא holds that one respect is normally enough, he needs the extra word to exclude this case. That is the word's job.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it / conclude from this
an animal born through the side wall (by caesarean section)
firstborn

steps.confusionAlert: This is רבינא's view, not the final הלכה. The גמרא is about to reject it.

phrases.english: Rather, conclude from it
that 'firstborn' comes to exclude
a case where one comes out after one born by caesarean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out the other option, it gives the real job of the word 'בכור'.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's view that a בכור לדבר אחד is a בכור, with the extra word serving as a special exclusion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word 'בכור' in the פסוק, which must exclude something not already covered by 'פטר רחם'.

steps.title: רב אחא concedes the male-after-male case works for רבינא
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי begins his challenge to רבינא. He first grants that the case of a caesarean male followed by a natural male works well under רבינא's approach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: If you think a firstborn in one respect is called a firstborn, that works well where a male came out by caesarean and then a male came out through the womb. That one is not holy, because this birth is excluded by the word 'firstborn'. It is a firstborn of the womb, but it is not a firstborn of the males.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא starts to challenge רבינא by first agreeing about one case. This is the setup ('תינח', 'it works well') for the real attack in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the male-then-male case, the second male is first of the womb but not first of the males. רבינא can say the extra word 'בכור' excludes it, so his view fits this case.

keyTerms.meaning: if it enters your mind / if you assume
a firstborn in only one respect
it works out well (sets up a 'but…')
birth
males

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
If it enters your mind
that a firstborn in one respect is a firstborn,
it works well where there came out
a male by caesarean
and a male through the womb,
that it is not holy,
because this birth is excluded by 'firstborn',
since it is a firstborn of the womb,
but it is not a firstborn of the males.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge against רבינא's derivation in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's view that בכור לדבר אחד הוי בכור and that the extra word excludes the case after a יוצא דופן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: it grants the one case that the single extra word can cover, preparing to show a second case left uncovered.

steps.title: The female-caesarean case breaks רבינא's approach
steps.stepSummary: If a female came out by caesarean and then a male came out naturally, that male is first of the males and first of the womb. Under רבינא's view nothing excludes him, so he should be holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where a female came out by caesarean and a male came out through the womb, it should be holy, since it is a firstborn of the males and a firstborn of the womb!
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the real attack. רב אחא shows a case that רבינא cannot explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This male is a בכור in two respects: first male and first from the womb. The only respect he lacks is being the first birth overall. רבינא already used the extra word for the male-after-male case, so nothing is left to exclude this one. Yet he is not holy, so רבינא's approach fails.

keyTerms.meaning: by way of the side wall (caesarean)
by way of the womb (natural birth)
let it be holy (it should be holy!)

phrases.english: But where a female came out
by caesarean
and a male through the womb
let it be holy,
since there is a firstborn of the males
and a firstborn of the womb!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּיָצְתָה נְקֵבָה דֶּרֶךְ דּוֹפֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up in step 3 ('תינח… אלא…').
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One extra word can exclude only one case. The female-caesarean case is left unexcluded, so under רבינא the male would be holy, but the הלכה is that he is not.

steps.title: The conclusion follows אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the correct view is אביי's: a בכור in only one respect is not a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that it is like אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on רבינא's approach and decides in favor of אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under אביי, 'בכור' means a firstborn in every respect. So both cases, male-then-male and female-then-male after a caesarean, are excluded without needing an extra word for each.

keyTerms.meaning: it is clear (the conclusion after rejecting an alternative)
אביי, whose view is accepted here

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows אביי: בכור לדבר אחד לא הוי בכור. An animal must be a firstborn in every respect to be holy as a בכור, so anything born after a יוצא דופן (male or female) is not a בכור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a בכור must be first in every way, which decides real cases of animals born after a caesarean sibling.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear: like Abaye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Results from the unanswered challenge in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בכור לדבר אחד לא הוי בכור, like אביי.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the perek הלוקח עובר פרתו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of the perek הלוקח עובר פרתו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'One who purchases the fetus of his cow'.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the perek. It is a closing formula, not an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הדרן עלך' expresses the learner's wish to come back and review the perek. The name of the perek comes from its opening words.

keyTerms.meaning: 'we will return to you': the formula for finishing a perek
name of the perek: 'One who buys the fetus of his cow'

phrases.english: We will return to you,
'One who purchases the fetus of his cow'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek after the final conclusion in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of the perek הלוקח עובר פרתו.

steps.title: New perek opens: buying an animal from a non-Jew and רבי ישמעאל's age rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents a case: an animal is bought from a גוי, and no one knows whether it already gave birth. רבי ישמעאל rules by age. A goat in its first year, a sheep in its second year, or a cow or donkey in its third year gives a definite בכור to the כהן. Past those ages, it is a ספק.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone buys an animal from a גוי and does not know whether it has given birth before or not. רבי ישמעאל says: a goat in its first year, its next male is definitely for the כהן; from then on it is a ספק. A sheep in its second year is definitely for the כהן; from then on it is a ספק. A cow or donkey in its third year is definitely for the כהן; from then on it is a ספק.
steps.whatsHappening: A new perek begins with a new case. Animals owned by a גוי are not subject to בכורה, so once a Jew buys one, we need to know whether its next male is the first from its womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל assumes each type of animal does not give birth before a certain age. If it was bought within that age, it surely never gave birth, and its next male is a definite בכור. Once it is older, it may have given birth already while it belonged to the גוי, so the status is a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
It has already had its first birth
Definitely belongs to the כהן
Doubtful case
From this point (age) onward

steps.confusionAlert: The ages refer to the mother at the time it was bought. They do not refer to the age of the newborn.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who buys an animal from a non-Jew,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אִם בִּיכְּרָה אִם לֹא בִּיכְּרָה.
phrases.english: and does not know whether it already gave birth or did not give birth.
Rabbi Yishmael says:
A goat in its first year: its offspring is definitely for the priest;
from then on, it is uncertain.
A sheep in its second year: definitely for the priest;
from then on, it is uncertain.

phrases.aramaic: פָּרָה וַחֲמוֹר בְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ — וַדַּאי לַכֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: A cow or donkey in its third year: definitely for the priest;
from then on, it is uncertain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This opens the new perek after the הדרן in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, an animal bought within the typical first-birth age gives a definite בכור. Past that age, the status is a ספק.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: Signs of pregnancy also free an animal from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects רבי ישמעאל's age rule. An animal is freed from בכורה not only by a full birth but also by signs of a pregnancy, and those can happen even when the animal is young.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: If an animal were freed only by giving birth to a full baby, you would be right. But the Sages said that the sign of a pregnancy is enough. In a small animal the sign is a murky discharge (טינוף). In a large animal it is an afterbirth (שליא). In a woman it is a fetal sac or an afterbirth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back on רבי ישמעאל. He says that age cannot prove the animal never "opened its womb."
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's "definite" category depends on the animal being too young to have given birth. רבי עקיבא points out that a miscarriage sign such as טינוף or שליא also counts as the first opening of the womb. That can happen within the first year, so even a young animal is not a definite case.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes exempt (from having a later בכור)
Small livestock (sheep, goats)
Large livestock (cows, donkeys)
Murky discharge from the womb
Afterbirth (placenta)
Fetal sac

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
If only by a full offspring
the animal were exempted, it would be as you say,
but the Sages said:
the sign of an offspring in a small animal is a murky discharge,
and in a large animal, an afterbirth,
and in a woman, a fetal sac or an afterbirth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אִילּוּ בְּוָולָד בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This directly rejects the reasoning behind רבי ישמעאל's "definite" category.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects רבי ישמעאל's claim that a young animal's next male is a definite בכור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי ישמעאל treats only a full birth as exempting. In fact, early signs of pregnancy also exempt, and these are possible at any age.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's general rule: known, unknown, and doubtful cases
steps.stepSummary: There are three outcomes. If the animal is known to have given birth, the כהן gets nothing. If it is known not to have given birth, the next male goes to the כהן. If it is a ספק, the owner eats it once it gets a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule. Whenever we know the animal already gave birth, the כהן gets nothing here. Whenever we know it did not give birth, the offspring goes to the כהן. If it is a ספק, the owner eats it once it has a מום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא replaces the age-based rule with a simple three-part rule based only on what is actually known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Age no longer creates a "definite" status. Only real knowledge does. In a ספק case the כהן cannot take the animal away from the owner, because he cannot prove it is a בכור. Since it might be holy, the owner may only eat it after it develops a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
Once it has a blemish (מום)
For the owners

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, only actual knowledge decides the status. A ספק stays with the owner and is eaten after it gets a מום.

phrases.english: This is the principle:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁבִּיכְּרָה — אֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: anywhere it is known that it gave birth, the priest has nothing here;

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה — הֲרֵי זֶה לַכֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: and anywhere it did not give birth, that goes to the priest;
and if it is uncertain, it is eaten by the owner once it has a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the age rule, רבי עקיבא gives his own positive rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Known birth means nothing for the כהן. Known no birth means it goes to the כהן. A ספק is eaten by the owner with a מום.

steps.title: Why only a ספק? Most animals give birth in their first year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל. Once a goat is past its first year, we should follow the רוב. Most animals get pregnant and give birth within their first year, so this one surely gave birth already, and its next male should not be a בכור at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From then on, why is it only a ספק? Go after the majority of animals. Most animals get pregnant and give birth within their first year, so this animal surely already gave birth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and attacks רבי ישמעאל's "ספק" category for older animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we rely on רוב. Most animals give birth within their first year, so an animal older than that should be treated as having definitely given birth. The כהן should then get nothing, and the case should not be a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
Why?
Follow the majority
It certainly gave birth

phrases.english: GEMARA: From then on, why is it uncertain?
Follow the majority of animals,
and most animals become pregnant and give birth
within their first year,
so this one certainly gave birth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This goes back to רבי ישמעאל's ruling in step 7 and questions his "ספק" category.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's ruling that an animal past the first-birth age is only a ספק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The principle of following the רוב should make it definite that the animal already gave birth, so it should not be a ספק.

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי ישמעאל holds like רבי מאיר and worries about the minority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tentatively suggests that רבי ישמעאל follows רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר takes the minority into account, so for him the רוב is not enough to remove the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבי ישמעאל holds like רבי מאיר, who is concerned about the minority?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible explanation for the question in step 10. This line sets up the next move, because the suggestion would put רבי ישמעאל against the רבנן, and the גמרא will respond to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי ישמעאל worries about the minority of animals that do not give birth in their first year, the רוב cannot settle the case, and it stays a ספק. But this would mean his view only works according to רבי מאיר, which is why the word "לימא" signals that the גמרא will probably reject it. The answer, "אפילו תימא רבנן," comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a tentative suggestion)
Is concerned about the minority
He holds

steps.confusionAlert: "לימא" is only a suggestion and not the conclusion. The גמרא goes on to say that רבי ישמעאל can agree even with the רבנן.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rabbi Yishmael
holds like Rabbi Meir,
who is concerned about the minority?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This offers a tentative resolution to the רוב challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tentative attribution: it ties רבי ישמעאל to רבי מאיר's position on the minority.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since most animals give birth in their first year, the רוב should make it definite.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tentatively, רבי ישמעאל worries about the מיעוט, like רבי מאיר, so the case stays a ספק. The גמרא will soon offer another answer.

steps.title: Even רבנן only follow a majority that is right in front of us
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רבי ישמעאל can agree with רבנן, because רבנן only follow a רוב that is present and countable, not a general pattern.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say רבי ישמעאל follows רבנן. רבנן only follow the majority when the majority is in front of us, like nine shops or a vote of the סנהדרין. But a majority that is not in front of us, רבנן do not follow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to explain רבי ישמעאל. He does not need to follow רבי מאיר, because even רבנן would not rely on this kind of majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of רוב. One is a majority you can actually see and count, like nine kosher shops against one non-kosher shop, or most judges voting one way. The other is a general pattern, like 'most goats give birth in their first year.' The claim here is that רבנן only rely on the first kind, so the challenge in Step 10 does not hurt רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. Introduces a new answer that works even under the other opinion.
A majority that is in front of us, one that is present and countable
A majority that is not in front of us, a general statistical pattern
Nine shops. The classic case of nine kosher meat shops and one non-kosher one.
The rabbinic high court, which follows the majority vote of its judges

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבנן reject the idea of רוב altogether. The claim is only that they limit it to a majority that is physically present.
steps.whyThisMatters: The split between a present majority and a non-present majority is a key tool all over ש״ס.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows the Rabbis,
when they go after the majority,
it is with a majority that is in front of us,
such as nine shops and the Sanhedrin,
phrases.notes: Both are majorities you can actually count.

phrases.english: but a majority that is not in front of us,
the Rabbis do not go after the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of Step 10, in place of the רבי מאיר answer of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between two types of majority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבנן follow every רוב, so רבי ישמעאל must follow רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן follow only a present majority. The age-based birth pattern is a non-present majority, so even רבנן would not rely on it.

steps.title: But רבנן do follow a non-present majority for minors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the distinction. In the case of a minor boy or girl, רבנן rely on a majority that is not in front of us.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the case of a minor boy and a minor girl. That is a majority that is not in front of us, and still רבנן follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. This line states the challenge, and the next steps bring the source to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said רבנן never rely on a non-present majority. Here the גמרא points to a case where they seem to do exactly that. If so, the second answer for רבי ישמעאל falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But look! A word that opens a challenge
A minor boy
A minor girl

phrases.english: But there is the case of a minor boy and a minor girl,
which is a majority that is not in front of us,
and the Rabbis do go after the majority,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction made in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבנן do not follow a רוב that is not in front of us
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a known case where רבנן rely on a non-present majority, so the distinction cannot be correct.

steps.title: The source: רבי מאיר forbids minors from doing חליצה and יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the source. רבי מאיר says minors do neither חליצה nor יבום. רבנן agree about חליצה because of a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: a minor boy and a minor girl do not do חליצה and do not do יבום. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The רבנן said to him: You are right that they do not do חליצה, because the word 'man' is written in that section of the Torah, and we compare the woman to the man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind its challenge. First it shows where רבי מאיר and רבנן agree, which is on חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that minors cannot do חליצה. The reason is a verse: the Torah says 'man,' meaning an adult, and the woman is compared to the man. This agreement has nothing to do with רוב. The real argument, about יבום, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned. Introduces a quoted tannaitic source.
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
Levirate marriage. The brother marries the widow of his brother who died childless.
Man, meaning an adult male
We compare. Two cases are linked to share the same law.

steps.confusionAlert: רבנן agree about חליצה only because of the word 'man' in the verse, not because of any worry about רוב. The argument about רוב is only about יבום.

phrases.english: As we learned:
A minor boy and a minor girl
do not do חליצה and do not do יבום;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: יָפֶה אָמַרְתָּ שֶׁאֵין חוֹלְצִין,
phrases.english: They said to him: You spoke well that they do not do חליצה,
since 'man' is written in the section,
and we compare the woman to the man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that backs up the challenge of Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That רבנן rely on a non-present majority
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רבי מאיר and רבנן about minors doing חליצה and יבום

steps.title: רבנן ask: why forbid יבום?
steps.stepSummary: Inside the source, רבנן ask רבי מאיר why minors may not do יבום, since no verse limits it to adults.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason they may not do יבום?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the quoted source, רבנן ask רבי מאיר for his reason about יבום. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חליצה there is a verse, but for יבום there is no word like 'man' that requires an adult. So רבנן want to know where רבי מאיר's ban on יבום comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
They do not do יבום

phrases.english: What is the reason they do not do יבום?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted source and moves from חליצה to יבום.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי מאיר's reason for forbidding minors to do יבום

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the child may turn out unable to have children
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר fears the boy may be a סריס or the girl an איילונית. Then there would be no מצוה of יבום, and the marriage would be a forbidden relationship.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: A minor boy might turn out to be a סריס. A minor girl might turn out to be an איילונית. Then they would end up in a forbidden relationship.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives his reason. He worries about the small chance that the child cannot have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום exists to build a family for the brother who died. If one side cannot have children, there is no מצוה, and a brother's wife is a forbidden relative (ערוה). Since we cannot yet know about a child, רבי מאיר worries about this minority case. This fits his view from Step 11 that he takes the minority into account.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, lest. Expresses a worry.
A man unable to father children
A woman unable to bear children
Come upon a forbidden relationship

steps.confusionAlert: Why would יבום be forbidden? A brother's wife is normally an ערוה. Only the מצוה of יבום permits her, and that מצוה does not apply if no children can come from the marriage.

phrases.english: He said to them:
A minor boy, lest he turn out to be a סריס;
a minor girl, lest she turn out to be an איילונית;
and they will turn out to have come upon a forbidden relationship.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר worries about the minority of children who cannot have children, because יבום with them would be a forbidden relationship.

steps.title: רבנן follow the majority of children, which is not in front of us
steps.stepSummary: רבנן permit יבום because most children are not unable to have children. That is a non-present majority, so the distinction from Step 12 seems wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן? Go after the majority of minor boys, and most minor boys are not סריסים. Go after minor girls, and most minor girls are not איילונית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. רבנן clearly rely on a majority that is not in front of us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Most children are not סריסים' is a general pattern. You cannot count it in front of you, exactly like 'most goats give birth in their first year.' Yet רבנן rely on it. So the claim in Step 12 that רבנן ignore a non-present majority looks false, and the second answer for רבי ישמעאל is in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Go after, follow
Not
They are

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן do follow a non-present majority, as in the case of minors and יבום. That knocks out the distinction offered in Step 12, and the גמרא will need a new answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows that the argument between רבי מאיר and רבנן about minority worries reaches even general statistical patterns, not only countable groups.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
Go after the majority of minor boys,
and most minor boys are not סריסים;
go after minor girls,
and most minor girls are not איילונית!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out רבנן's reasoning from the source and completes the challenge begun in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction of Step 12 between a present and a non-present majority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבנן rely on the general fact that most children can have children. That is a non-present majority, so they do follow such a רוב, and the answer for רבי ישמעאל fails.

steps.title: רבא begins a new explanation
steps.stepSummary: The word אלא tells us the earlier distinction has been dropped. The גמרא now turns to רבא for a fresh explanation.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא drops the explanation that was just challenged and introduces רבא, whose actual answer comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 showed that רבנן rely on a majority that is not in front of us, as in the case of minors and יבום. That broke the distinction from Step 12. The word אלא admits that distinction failed and clears the way for רבא to explain things a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather / instead. It signals that the previous explanation has been rejected and a new one is coming.
רבא said. This introduces the statement of the אמורא רבא.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not expect רבא's answer in this line. These words only introduce it, and the content comes next.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
phrases.notes: אלא marks the rejection of the distinction from Step 12, which Step 17 disproved. רבא's new explanation follows on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It responds to the קשיא in Step 17 by dropping the challenged distinction and introducing a new explanation from רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the explanation: a new approach replaces the rejected distinction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We first thought רבנן rely only on a majority that is in front of us, not on one that is absent.
steps.terutzMaskana: That distinction has been dropped. רבא's new explanation follows on the next amud.
